title_en: Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, and Ministry of Public Security — Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Organizing and Leading Pyramid Scheme Activities
keywords_en: criminal case of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court   Supreme People's Procuratorate   Ministry of Public Security

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Organizing and Leading Pyramid Scheme Activities

Gongtongzi [2013] No. 37

High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and Public Security Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; Military Court and Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; People's Procuratorate and Public Security Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

To address the issues encountered by public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts in handling criminal cases of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities, and to lawfully punish the crime of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities, in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law, and in light of judicial practice, the following opinions are hereby put forward regarding the application of law in handling criminal cases of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities:

1. Regarding the Determination of the Number of Levels and Participants in a Pyramid Scheme Organization

Where, under the pretext of selling commodities or providing services and other business activities, a pyramid scheme organization requires participants to pay fees or purchase commodities or services to obtain qualifications for joining, forms levels in a certain order, directly or indirectly uses the number of persons developed as the basis for calculating remuneration or rebates, induces or coerces participants to continue developing others to join, defrauds property, and disrupts the economic and social order, if the number of participants in the pyramid scheme activities within the organization is 30 persons or more and the number of levels is three or more, the organizers and leaders shall be criminally liable.

Where a person organizes and leads multiple pyramid scheme organizations, and the levels in a single organization or multiple organizations have reached three or more, the numbers of persons developed in each organization may be calculated cumulatively.

Where an organizer or leader formally withdraws from the original pyramid scheme organization but continues to receive remuneration or rebates from the original organization, the number of levels and persons developed by the original organization after his or her withdrawal shall be counted as the levels and persons he or she developed.

In handling criminal cases of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities, if it is truly impossible due to objective conditions to collect verbal evidence from each participant in the pyramid scheme activities one by one, the criminal facts such as the number of participants and the number of levels may be comprehensively determined based on evidence such as records of payments and fees collected and verified in accordance with law, records of remuneration and rebates, audio-visual materials, relationship diagrams of pyramid scheme participants, bank account transaction records, internet electronic data, and expert opinions.

2. Regarding the Determination and Handling of Persons Involved in Pyramid Scheme Activities

The following persons may be determined as organizers or leaders of pyramid scheme activities:

(1) Persons who play the roles of initiating, planning, or manipulating in the pyramid scheme activities;

(2) Persons who assume responsibilities such as management or coordination in the pyramid scheme activities;

(3) Persons who assume responsibilities such as publicity or training in the pyramid scheme activities;

(4) Persons who have previously received criminal punishment for organizing or leading pyramid scheme activities, or have received administrative punishment for organizing or leading pyramid scheme activities within one year, and have directly or indirectly developed 15 or more participants in pyramid scheme activities with three or more levels;

(5) Other persons who play a key role in the implementation of the pyramid scheme activities or the establishment and expansion of the pyramid scheme organization.

Where the crime of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities is committed in the name of a unit, persons who, under the assignment of the unit, only engage in labor-type work shall generally not be subject to criminal liability.

3. Regarding the Determination of "Defrauding Property"

Where the organizer or leader of pyramid scheme activities fabricates or distorts national policies, fabricates or exaggerates business, investment, or service projects and profit prospects, conceals the true source of remuneration or rebates, or uses other fraudulent means, and carries out the acts described in Article 224a of the Criminal Law, and illegally profits from fees paid by participants in the pyramid scheme activities or from expenses for purchasing commodities or services, it shall be determined as defrauding property. Whether the participants in the pyramid scheme activities consider themselves defrauded does not affect the determination of defrauding property.

4. Regarding the Determination of "Serious Circumstances"

Where an organizer or leader of a pyramid scheme organization that meets the conditions specified in paragraph 1 of Article 1 of these Opinions has any of the following circumstances, it shall be determined as "serious circumstances" as stipulated in Article 224a of the Criminal Law:

(1) The cumulative number of participants in the pyramid scheme activities organized or led reaches 120 persons or more;

(2) The cumulative amount of pyramid scheme funds directly or indirectly collected from participants in the pyramid scheme activities reaches RMB 2.5 million or more;

(3) Has previously received criminal punishment for organizing or leading pyramid scheme activities, or has received administrative punishment for organizing or leading pyramid scheme activities within one year, and has directly or indirectly developed a cumulative total of 60 or more participants in the pyramid scheme activities;

(4) Causes serious consequences such as mental breakdown or suicide among participants in the pyramid scheme activities;

(5) Causes other serious consequences or adverse social impact.

5. Regarding the Handling of "Group Commission" Activities

Where the organizer or leader of pyramid scheme activities, by developing persons, requires the developed persons to develop other persons to join, forming an up-line and down-line relationship, and calculates and pays remuneration to the up-line based on the sales performance of the down-line, thereby obtaining illegal benefits, this constitutes a "group commission" type of pyramid scheme activity.

A purely "group commission" type of pyramid scheme activity aimed at selling commodities and using sales performance as the basis for calculating remuneration shall not be treated as a crime. Where the forms of "group commission" are adopted, but the activity is essentially a pyramid scheme activity that "uses the number of persons developed as the basis for calculating remuneration or rebates," it shall be convicted and punished as the crime of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities in accordance with Article 224a of the Criminal Law.

6. Regarding the Application of Charges

Where, for the purpose of illegal possession, a person organizes or leads pyramid scheme activities and simultaneously constitutes the crime of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities and the crime of fundraising fraud, the offense with the heavier punishment shall be applied for conviction and punishment.

Where, while committing the crime of organizing and leading pyramid scheme activities, a person also commits acts such as intentional injury, unlawful detention, extortion, obstructing official duties, gathering a crowd to disturb social order, gathering a crowd to storm state organs, gathering a crowd to disturb public order at public places or traffic order, and such acts constitute crimes, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions on concurrent punishment for multiple offenses.

The terms "or more" and "within" used in these Opinions include the number itself.

The terms "levels" and "tiers" used in these Opinions refer to the hierarchical relationship of up-line and down-line between the organizer or leader and the participants in the pyramid scheme activities, and not to the status grade of the organizer or leader within the pyramid scheme organization.

The calculation of the number of persons and levels within a pyramid scheme organization, as well as the calculation of the number of persons and levels directly or indirectly developed by the organizer or leader among the participants, shall include the organizer or leader himself or herself and the level to which they belong.

November 14, 2013
